title: Salary vs department average
task: Set result to employees (with a salary) plus a column vs_dept_avg = salary − department mean salary, rounded to 0 dp; keep emp_id, dept_id, salary, vs_dept_avg.

title: Percent of department payroll
task: Set result to a DataFrame emp_id, dept_id, pct_of_dept (salary / dept total salary * 100, 2 dp) for employees with a salary.

title: Salary quartiles
task: Set result to a DataFrame emp_id, salary, quartile (1 = highest paid) using pd.qcut on salary into 4 bins, for employees with a salary, sorted by emp_id.
answer:
e = employees.dropna(subset=['salary']).copy()
e['quartile'] = pd.qcut(e['salary'], 4, labels=[4, 3, 2, 1]).astype(int)
result = e[['emp_id', 'salary', 'quartile']].sort_values('emp_id').reset_index(drop=True)

title: Retention by hire year
task: Set result to a Series indexed by hire year with the % of that cohort still Active (1 dp), sorted by year.

title: Average tenure of leavers by year
context: Tenure at exit, grouped by exit year.
task: Set result to a Series of mean tenure in days for employees who left, grouped by exit year, rounded to 0 dp, sorted by year.
hint: Filter Left, compute tenure, groupby exit year.

title: Reviews trend per employee
task: Set result to a DataFrame emp_id, first_rating, last_rating for employees with 2+ reviews, where last_rating < first_rating (rating declined). Order reviews by year.
hint: sort by year, groupby first()/last(), filter counts.
answer:
r = reviews.sort_values(['emp_id', 'year'])
g = r.groupby('emp_id')['rating'].agg(first_rating='first', last_rating='last', n='count')
result = g[(g['n'] >= 2) & (g['last_rating'] < g['first_rating'])][['first_rating', 'last_rating']].reset_index()

title: Average rating by dept and year
task: Set result to a pivot_table: index dept name, columns year, values mean rating (2 dp), fill_value 0.
answer:
m = reviews.merge(employees[['emp_id', 'dept_id']], on='emp_id').merge(departments[['dept_id', 'dept']], on='dept_id')
result = m.pivot_table(index='dept', columns='year', values='rating', aggfunc='mean', fill_value=0).round(2)

title: Adjusted gender pay gap
task: Set result to a Series indexed by level of (mean male salary − mean female salary) rounded to 0 dp, only levels having both genders.
hint: pivot_table mean by level×gender, dropna, subtract.
answer:
p = employees.pivot_table(index='level', columns='gender', values='salary', aggfunc='mean').dropna()
result = (p['M'] - p['F']).round()

title: Pay for performance
task: Set result to the Pearson correlation between an employee's mean rating and salary (2 dp), over employees having both.
hint: Build a table of mean rating + salary, .corr().

title: Leave overlapping a month
task: Set result to the number of leave rows whose date range (start_date to start_date + days − 1) includes any day in March 2025 (an int).
hint: end = start + days-1; overlap if start <= Mar31 and end >= Mar1.

title: Rank employees company-wide
task: Set result to the 3 highest-paid employees as a DataFrame name, salary, rank (dense, 1=highest), for employees with a salary.
answer:
e = employees.dropna(subset=['salary']).copy()
e['rank'] = e['salary'].rank(ascending=False, method='dense').astype(int)
result = e[e['rank'] <= 3].sort_values(['rank', 'name'])[['name', 'salary', 'rank']].reset_index(drop=True)

title: Manager team average salary
task: Set result to a Series indexed by manager_id of the mean salary of their direct reports (0 dp), for managers with reports.

title: Managers paid less than a report
context: Compare manager to their team max.
task: Set result to a Series of manager_id where at least one direct report earns more than the manager.
hint: Join reports' salary to manager salary and compare max.
answer:
sal = employees.set_index('emp_id')['salary']
rep = employees.dropna(subset=['manager_id', 'salary']).copy()
rep['mgr_salary'] = rep['manager_id'].map(sal)
g = rep.groupby('manager_id').apply(lambda d: (d['salary'] > d['mgr_salary']).any())
result = pd.Series(g[g].index)

title: Compa-ratio
task: Set result to employees (with salary) plus compa_ratio = salary / level median salary, rounded to 2 dp; keep emp_id, level, compa_ratio.

title: Top earners = 50% of payroll
task: Set result to the number of highest-paid employees whose cumulative salary first reaches 50% of total payroll (an int).
hint: sort desc, cumsum / total, count where cumulative < 0.5 then +1.
answer:
s = employees['salary'].dropna().sort_values(ascending=False)
cum = s.cumsum() / s.sum()
result = int((cum.shift(fill_value=0) < 0.5).sum())

title: Ratings wide by year
task: Set result to a DataFrame indexed by emp_id with one column per year (2022,2023,2024) holding that year's rating, for employees who have all three years.
answer:
p = reviews.pivot_table(index='emp_id', columns='year', values='rating')
result = p.dropna()

title: Anniversary this quarter
task: Set result to the number of active employees whose hire month is in Q3 (Jul, Aug or Sep) (an int).

title: Headcount change by year
task: Set result to a Series indexed by year (2018-2024) of net headcount change = hires that year − exits that year, sorted by year.
hint: Two value_counts by year, reindex to a common range, subtract.
answer:
yrs = list(range(2018, 2025))
hires = employees['hire_date'].dt.year.value_counts().reindex(yrs, fill_value=0)
exits = employees['exit_date'].dropna().dt.year.value_counts().reindex(yrs, fill_value=0)
result = (hires - exits).astype(int)

title: Median salary per department
task: Set result to a Series of median salary per dept name (0 dp), sorted descending.

title: Salary z-scores
task: Set result to the number of employees whose salary z-score (population std) exceeds 2 in absolute value (an int; ignore missing).
answer:
x = employees['salary'].dropna().to_numpy()
z = (x - x.mean()) / x.std()
result = int((np.abs(z) > 2).sum())

title: Salary percentiles
task: Set result to a list of the 25th, 50th and 90th salary percentiles (0 dp each), ignoring missing.

title: Promotion after low rating
task: Set result to the number of employees who were promoted in a year immediately after a year with rating <= 2 (an int).
hint: sort by year, shift rating within emp, check promoted & prev<=2.
answer:
r = reviews.sort_values(['emp_id', 'year']).copy()
r['prev'] = r.groupby('emp_id')['rating'].shift()
result = int(((r['promoted'] == 1) & (r['prev'] <= 2)).sum())

title: Duplicate names
task: Set result to a Series of full names that occur more than once, with their counts, sorted descending by count.

title: Reviews without an active employee
task: Set result to the number of review rows whose emp_id is not present in employees (an int).

title: Above-median flag per level
task: Set result to the number of employees paid strictly above their level's median salary (an int).
answer:
e = employees.dropna(subset=['salary'])
med = e.groupby('level')['salary'].transform('median')
result = int((e['salary'] > med).sum())

title: Leave rate per department
task: Set result to a Series of leave days per employee (total days / headcount, 2 dp) per dept name.
hint: days per dept via merge, divide by headcount.
answer:
m = leave.merge(employees[['emp_id', 'dept_id']], on='emp_id').merge(departments[['dept_id', 'dept']], on='dept_id')
days = m.groupby('dept')['days'].sum()
hc = employees.merge(departments, on='dept_id').groupby('dept').size()
result = (days / hc).round(2).dropna()

title: Tenure bucket distribution
task: Set result to a Series of counts per tenure bucket using pd.cut on tenure years with bins [0,2,5,10,50] and labels ['<2','2-5','5-10','10+'].
answer:
ty = (pd.Timestamp('2025-07-31') - employees['hire_date']).dt.days / 365
b = pd.cut(ty, bins=[0, 2, 5, 10, 50], labels=['<2', '2-5', '5-10', '10+'])
result = b.value_counts().sort_index()

title: Department summary
task: Set result to a DataFrame indexed by dept name with headcount, avg_salary (0 dp) and attrition_pct (1 dp), sorted by dept.
hint: merge, groupby.agg with a lambda for attrition.
answer:
m = employees.merge(departments, on='dept_id')
result = m.groupby('dept').agg(headcount=('emp_id', 'count'), avg_salary=('salary', 'mean')).round()
result['attrition_pct'] = (m.assign(left=(m['status'] == 'Left')).groupby('dept')['left'].mean() * 100).round(1)
result = result.sort_index()

title: Second highest paid per level
task: Set result to a Series indexed by level of the second-highest salary in each level (0 dp).

title: Longest-serving active employee
task: Set result to the name of the active employee with the earliest hire_date.

title: Consistent top performers
task: Set result to a Series of emp_id who have 2+ reviews and every review rating >= 4.
hint: groupby with min rating and count.

title: Headcount by level and gender
task: Set result to a DataFrame of counts with index level and columns gender (unstack of a groupby size), fill missing with 0.

title: Salary gap to top of level
task: Set result to a DataFrame emp_id, level, gap_to_top = level max salary − salary (0 dp), for employees with a salary, keeping only rows where gap_to_top > 0.
